b: Partial (nephron-sparing) nephrectomy: the standard treatment for T1 tumours (under 7 cm) , especially under 4 cm, a solitary kidney, bilateral tumours, or a predisposition to further tumours (VHL), because it preserves renal function and g

Radical nephrectomy (open or laparoscopic ) for larger or more complex tumours: removal of the whole kidney with Gerota's fascia and the perinephric fat (and the ipsilateral adrenal when involved or the tumour is in the upper pole) . Laparo
Regional lymph node dissection (for clinically enlarged nodes; staging value only).
Tumour thrombus in the renal vein or IVC: radical nephrectomy with thrombectomy (cardiac bypass for thrombus above the diaphragm).
Active surveillance for small renal masses (under 3 to 4 cm) that grow slowly, in elderly or unfit patients.

snip.t: Localised disease: organ-preserving surgery whenever possible: circumcision (for prepuce-only tumours), wide local excision, glans resurfacing or glansectomy with reconstruction, Mohs surgery, laser ablation (CO2 or Nd:YAG) for Tis and Ta, topical therapy for Tis.
